claims.text: The feedstock is cobalt-free AlCrFeNiSi powder.
Optimized LPBF laser scanning strategies will reduce thermal gradients during solidification.
Reduced thermal gradients will decrease compositional segregation.
Reduced thermal gradients will decrease residual stresses.
Reduced thermal gradients will decrease defect formation.
Decreased segregation, residual stress, and defect formation will improve mechanical integrity relative to conventional fabrication.
The optimized scanning strategy lowers energy input per unit area.
Lower energy input per unit area reduces temperature gradients during melting and solidification.
Decreasing rapid-cooling effects minimizes residual stresses.
Decreasing rapid-cooling effects limits defect formation.
Optimized LPBF processing will produce higher tensile or yield strength than conventional fabrication.
Optimized LPBF processing will produce higher ductility than conventional fabrication.
Optimized LPBF processing will produce lower residual stress than conventional fabrication.
Optimized LPBF processing will produce fewer microstructural defects than conventional fabrication.
The hypothesis is valid for LPBF of cobalt-free AlCrFeNiSi under controlled inert conditions at room temperature.
Different energy densities, powder characteristics, or atmospheric conditions may alter the results.

contradictions.description: The stated baseline is conventionally fabricated AlCrFeNiSi, whereas the experiment compares two LPBF groups using optimized versus conventional scanning parameters. This does not directly test the claimed comparison against conventional non-LPBF fabrication.
